<laravel-boost-guidelines>
Laravel app: laravel/fortify v1, laravel/framework v12, laravel/prompts v0, laravel/socialite v5, livewire/flux v2, livewire/livewire v4, laravel/boost v2, laravel/mcp v0, laravel/pail v1, laravel/pint v1, laravel/sail v1, pestphp/pest v4, phpunit/phpunit v12.

Activate relevant skills: `fluxui-development` for Flux/UI; `livewire-development` for Livewire; `pest-testing` for tests; `tailwindcss-development` for styling; `developing-with-fortify` for authentication/Fortify.

Follow conventions; inspect siblings; use descriptive names, existing components and directories. Do not change dependencies without approval. Do not create verification scripts or tinker when tests cover that functionality and prove they work. You must only create documentation files if explicitly requested by the user. Be concise.

Use Boost MCP tools: `list-artisan-commands` for Artisan parameters; `get-absolute-url` for URLs; `tinker` for PHP/Eloquent debugging; `database-query` read-only; `database-schema` before migrations/models; `browser-logs` for recent logs. Always use `search-docs` before code changes for version-specific Laravel/ecosystem documentation; broad topics, multiple queries as useful, no package names. Query syntax: word search auto-stems; space means AND; quoted phrases require adjacency; mixed terms combine AND; multiple queries mean ANY.

If frontend changes are not reflected, ask the user to run `npm run build`, `npm run dev`, or `composer run dev`. If Vite manifest errors occur, run `npm run build` or ask the user to run `npm run dev` or `composer run dev`.

Always use curly braces for control structures, including single-line bodies. Use PHP 8 constructor property promotion (`public function __construct(public GitHub $github) { }`). Do not allow empty `__construct()` methods with zero parameters unless the constructor is private. Always declare explicit return types and parameter type hints. Prefer TitleCase Enum keys, PHPDoc blocks over inline comments, and useful array-shape definitions. Never use comments within the code itself unless the logic is exceptionally complex.

Every change must be programmatically tested: write/update a test and run affected tests. Run minimum tests with `php artisan test --compact` plus filename/filter. Run `vendor/bin/pint --dirty --format agent` before finalizing. Do not run `vendor/bin/pint --test --format agent`, simply run `vendor/bin/pint --format agent` to fix any formatting issues.

Laravel: Use `php artisan make:` with `--no-interaction` and correct `--options`; `php artisan make:class` for generic classes. Use typed Eloquent relationships, models/relationships and `Model::query()` over raw queries; avoid `DB::`; prevent N+1 with eager loading; query builder only for complex operations. New models should include useful factories/seeders; ask whether needed and use `list-artisan-commands` to check `php artisan make:model` options. Use API Resources/versioning unless conventions differ. Always create Form Request classes with rules/custom messages, following siblings. Use built-in auth/authorization, named routes and `route()`. Queue time-consuming work with `ShouldQueue`. Use environment variables only in config files; never use `env()` directly outside config files; use `config('app.name')`, not `env('APP_NAME')`. Use factories/existing states and Faker style. Create feature tests with `php artisan make:test [options] {name}`; unit tests with `--unit`; most tests feature tests.

Laravel 12: middleware in `bootstrap/app.php` via `Application::configure()->withMiddleware()`; it registers middleware, exceptions and routing. Providers: `bootstrap/providers.php`; `app\Console\Kernel.php` no longer exists; use `bootstrap/app.php` or `routes/console.php`. Commands in `app/Console/Commands/` auto-available. When modifying a column, include all previously defined attributes or they will be dropped. Limit eager-loaded records with `$query->latest()->limit(10);`. Prefer a model `casts()` method when consistent.

Flux: Free components/variants, not Pro. Use `<flux:*>` when available.

Livewire: Use Alpine.js only when client-side interaction requires it; state stays server-side and actions validate/authorize.

Pest: Create tests: `php artisan make:test --pest {name}`. Run tests: `php artisan test --compact` or `php artisan test --compact --filter=testName`. Do NOT delete tests without approval. CRITICAL: ALWAYS use `search-docs` tool for version-specific Pest documentation and updated code examples.

Tailwind: Use existing conventions. IMPORTANT: Always use `search-docs` tool for version-specific Tailwind CSS documentation and updated code examples. Never rely on training data.

Fortify: Headless authentication with routes/controllers. IMPORTANT: Always use `search-docs` for detailed Laravel Fortify patterns/documentation.
</laravel-boost-guidelines>
